question: Which of the following is a characteristic property of a material?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Resistivity**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Resistivity** is a **characteristic property of a material** as it depends solely on the material and not on its shape or size.
 
• It is defined as the **inherent opposition** of a material to the flow of electric current. The formula for resistivity is: **ρ = R × A / L**, where:
 
 
• ρ is the resistivity of the material.
 
• R is the resistance.
 
• A is the cross-sectional area.
 
• L is the length of the conductor.
 
 
 
• Unlike resistance, which depends on the material's dimensions, resistivity is a **fixed property** for a specific material at a given temperature.
 
• Resistivity is measured in **ohm-meters (Ω·m)** in the SI system.
 
• It is used to classify materials as **conductors** (low resistivity), **semiconductors** (moderate resistivity), and **insulators** (high resistivity).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Resistance:**

 
 
• Resistance is the measure of how much a material opposes the flow of electric current. It depends on the material's **resistivity**, its dimensions (length and cross-sectional area), and the temperature.
 
• The formula for resistance is **R = ρ × L / A**, where ρ is resistivity, L is length, and A is cross-sectional area.
 
• Resistance is measured in **ohms (Ω)**.
 
 
 
• **Voltage:**
 
 
• Voltage is the **electric potential difference** between two points. It is the driving force that pushes current through a circuit.
 
• It is measured in **volts (V)**.
 
• Voltage depends on the power supply or source and not on the material's properties.
 
 
 
• **Current:**
 
 
• Current is the flow of electric charge through a conductor. It is measured in **amperes (A)**.
 
• It depends on the **voltage** across the conductor and the **resistance** of the material, as described by Ohm's Law: **I = V / R**.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Resistivity:**
 
 
• Resistivity is used in designing electrical components like **resistors** and **heating elements**.
 
• It helps in selecting materials for specific applications (e.g., copper for wires due to low resistivity, rubber for insulation due to high resistivity).
 
• Resistivity measurements are also used in **geophysics** to identify different types of rocks and minerals.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Temperature Dependence:**

 
 
• Resistivity of most materials **increases with temperature** (e.g., metals).
 
• In semiconductors, resistivity **decreases with temperature**, making them useful for temperature sensors.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Materials and Resistivity:**
 
 
• **Silver:** Lowest resistivity among metals (highly conductive).
 
• **Rubber:** High resistivity (excellent insulator).
 
• **Silicon:** Moderate resistivity (semiconductor).
 
 
 
• **Ohm's Law:** The relationship between voltage (V), current (I), and resistance (R) is given by **V = I × R**.
